neighbours.label: An -ing verbal noun used as a mass noun for an ongoing activity (some cutting, much crying, all this traveling, rumor-mongering); an ordinary mass noun in the same slot stays quiet
fire: There was some shouting in the hallway before the bell.
You don't hear much singing in this part of town.
All this packing has worn me out completely.
There was a lot of finger-pointing and bickering after the loss.
Cats often engage in scratching and tail-flicking.
Some digging is needed before the pipe can be fixed.
There will be no more cheating on the exam.
He hates all the hand-wringing and name-calling.
quiet: There was some paint in the hallway before the bell.
You don't hear much traffic in this part of town.
All this furniture has worn me out completely.
There was a lot of mud and rubbish after the flood.
Cats often sleep in baskets and on sofas.
Some gravel is needed before the pipe can be fixed.
There will be no more paper on the exam.
He hates all the noise and smoke.

short: -ing verbal noun as a mass noun
notes: Card: ' cutting', ' much', 'ong' of mongering, ' this' before traveling, ' tail' of tail-chasing. Logit effect promotes -ing words (' plotting', ' scrambling', ' dancing', ' mixing'). Probe: rumor-mongering 0.71, tail-chasing 0.65, traveling 0.43, crying 0.41, cutting 0.40; 'some wood' 0.02, 'much water' 0.10, 'all this luggage' 0.19, verb 'likes cutting wood' 0.01.
